direct_fact_uses.text:
[F1] For a hyperplane inclusion $i:\mathbb P^{r-1}\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^r$, multiplication by its defining linear form gives the exact holomorphic sequences
$0\to\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O\to i_*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}\to0$ and
$0\to\mathcal O(-2)\to\mathcal O(-1)\to i_*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}(-1)\to0$.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-hyperplane-twist-sequences]]

proof_steps.claim: Fix $r\in\{1,2,3\}$. In the first sequence of [F1], the map $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O)$ is restriction of constants and hence is the identity $\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$. Exactness therefore gives $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(-1))=0$. The adjacent higher groups of $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}$ vanish by [A1]; the long exact sequence then gives $H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q>0$.

Fix $r\in\{2,3\}$. In the second sequence of [F1], both $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}(-1)$ are acyclic by step 1.1, since $r-1\in\{1,2\}$. Its long exact cohomology sequence therefore gives $H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, including the stated $\mathbb P^3$ groups.

direct_fact_uses.text:
[F10] For each integer $m$, the analytic hyperplane sequence is
$0\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m-1)\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m)\to i_*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}(m)\to0$.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-hyperplane-twist-sequences]]

proof_steps.claim: First the holomorphic monad maps have homogeneous linear entries. Indeed, in the $m=1$ sequence of [F10], $H^1(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ by [A1], so restriction $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(1))\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O(1))$ is surjective and its kernel is the defining hyperplane coordinate times $H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$. Starting with $r=0$, where $\mathcal O(1)$ on a point has one-dimensional section space, induction shows that every section is a linear combination of the homogeneous coordinates: subtract the global coordinate lifts of its restriction, then the remaining section is a constant multiple of the defining coordinate. This applies to entries of both $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1))$. Thus no algebraic/analytic comparison is needed to introduce their four coefficient maps. By [A1] and [F9], the hyperplane sequences and analytic scalar theorem give exactly the negative-twist vanishings required by [F1]. Apply [F1] to the pairing isomorphism; it gives the unique constant Hermitian lift $H$ with the signed identities there. Thus no algebraic cohomology group is being substituted for the analytic lifting groups.

direct_fact_uses.text:
[F5] For these raw coefficients, affine injectivity of $a_z$ is equivalent to
costability, affine surjectivity of $b_z^\dagger$ is equivalent to stability,
and zero moments plus regularity give the displayed homogeneous bundle monad.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-rank-stability-criterion]]

proof_steps.claim: On the affine chart $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2] =[1:0:z_1:z_2]$, the raw maps are $a_z$ and $b_z^\dagger$ from [F5]. Since the original $\alpha,\beta$ have their required ranks at every point, [F5] gives costability and stability. Thus the extracted zero-moment datum is regular. Conversely, for stable and costable data, [F5] proves full homogeneous rank, composition zero, and local splitting, so the raw formula does define the required monad.

For any such raw datum and finite $z$, write $a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T$ and $b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,B_1-z_1,I)$. The two moment equations give $b_z^\dagger a_z=0$ and $a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z=:f_z$. Regularity makes both maps full rank, so $f_z$ is positive definite. On $\ell_z$ the monad is $\alpha=a_z\lambda_1+b_z\lambda_2$ and $\beta=b_z^\dagger\lambda_1-a_z^\dagger\lambda_2$. The cross Gram terms vanish, and $a_z,b_z$ identify two orthogonal copies of $V$ after applying $f_z^{-1/2}$. In these orthonormal coordinates the end maps on the first two copies are $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)^T$ and $(-\lambda_2,\lambda_1)$, the Euler complex $V\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V)\mathcal O\to V\mathcal O(1)$; the complementary term is $E_z\mathcal O$. Hence $H^0(F|_{\ell_z})=E_z$ with its positive induced form, and $F|_{\ell_z}$ is trivial. At infinity the same calculation in step 4.1 gives $W\otimes\mathcal O$ and its framing. The maps in step 6.1 are exactly the required locally split end maps.

direct_fact_uses.text: [F2] A linear monad morphism with its specified map on middle cohomology has the unique chain lift from the preceding lemma; its sigma-dual identities are $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and $\beta(jz)^\dagger=-H\alpha(z)$. [[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-chain-lift]]

proof_steps.claim: If $l\in L$, then $\beta(z)l=0$ for all $z$. By [F2], $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$, so $H(l,\alpha(jz)u)=0$ for every $u$ and $z$; since $j$ is bijective, $l\perp_H M$. Conversely, if $s\perp_H M$, then $\alpha(jz)^\dagger Hs=0$ for every $z$, hence $\beta(z)s=0$ and $s\in L$. Thus $L=M^{\perp_H}$, and nondegeneracy of $H$ gives $M=L^{\perp_H}$.

direct_fact_uses.text:
[F1] Under the negative-twist vanishings derived from [A1], every holomorphic
map of the stated monad cohomology bundles lifts uniquely to a constant chain
map; the signed self-dual lift is Hermitian and obeys
$\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and
$\beta(jz)^\dagger=-H\alpha(z)$.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-chain-lift]]

proof_steps.claim: First the holomorphic monad maps have homogeneous linear entries. Indeed, in the $m=1$ sequence of [F10], $H^1(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ by [A1], so restriction $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(1))\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O(1))$ is surjective and its kernel is the defining hyperplane coordinate times $H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$. Starting with $r=0$, where $\mathcal O(1)$ on a point has one-dimensional section space, induction shows that every section is a linear combination of the homogeneous coordinates: subtract the global coordinate lifts of its restriction, then the remaining section is a constant multiple of the defining coordinate. This applies to entries of both $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1))$. Thus no algebraic/analytic comparison is needed to introduce their four coefficient maps. By [A1] and [F9], the hyperplane sequences and analytic scalar theorem give exactly the negative-twist vanishings required by [F1]. Apply [F1] to the pairing isomorphism; it gives the unique constant Hermitian lift $H$ with the signed identities there. Thus no algebraic cohomology group is being substituted for the analytic lifting groups.

For the algebraic $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$ family category, [F11] directly supplies the needed $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(-2)$ groups over $A$ and $H^0(\mathcal O_A)=A$. Separately, on the analytic first-order thickening each twist has the split underlying analytic sheaf $\mathcal O_A(d)=\mathcal O(d)\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O(d)$; finite direct sums commute with sheaf cohomology, so [F9] gives the same vanishings there. Thus a holomorphic family pairing can be lifted analytically, whereas algebraic family sheaves use [F11]; neither computation substitutes algebraic cohomology for an analytic group or invokes GAGA. Both yield constant $A$-valued chain maps. In both categories the two kernel/image sequences identify global sections with the same constant coefficient kernel of $\beta_A$, so the specified global-section base-change condition is respected by this identification. Repeating the obstruction and ambiguity calculation of [F1] over these coefficient modules lifts the family pairing uniquely to an $A$-linear constant chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle matrix $H_A$; its inverse exists because its reduction is invertible. Global section base change identifies $H^0(F_A)$ with the constant coefficient kernel $L_A$ in $S_A$. Its reduction is injective, so a full-rank minor is a unit and $L_A$ is a direct summand.

By hypothesis the coefficient-image module $M_A$ is a direct summand. The coefficient identities give $M_A^\perp=L_A$; for a direct summand in a finite free module with a perfect pairing, the restriction map to its dual is split-surjective, so taking orthogonal complements twice returns that summand. Hence $M_A=L_A^\perp$ and $S_A=L_A\oplus M_A$. The line-section base change and the vanishing $H^0(\ell_A,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ make restriction of $L_A$ injective; the reduced line positivity makes $H_A|_{L_0}$ positive. The internal-positivity proof applies to the reduction on $M_0$, so its reduced form is positive too. On infinity the family framing identifies the remaining orthogonal complement isometrically with $W_A$.
